page-better-life-framework-description: Use this resource to help you understand more about each level and build empathy for yourself and the people around you.
page-better-life-framework-filters-descr: Use Filters To Focus On The Relevant Perspectives You Want To Understand.
page-better-life-framework-profile-1-tit: Happiness Is Getting What I Need
page-better-life-framework-profile-1-des: Once I get what I need, I will be happy.
page-better-life-framework-profile-2-tit: Happiness Is Getting What I Want
page-better-life-framework-profile-2-des: The more I get what I want, the happier I will become.
page-better-life-framework-profile-3-tit: Happiness Is Learning From My Experiences
page-better-life-framework-profile-3-des: If I can find the correct view of the world, I will be happy.
page-better-life-framework-profile-4-des: The more we are free to do what we want, without hurting others, the happier we will be.
page-better-life-framework-profile-5-des: It's not about me, its about we. Fulfillment comes when I am my best self and contributing to others.
page-better-life-framework-level-1-descr: Life is about dealing with my needs and feeling good by getting what I need.
page-better-life-framework-level-1-unloc: I feel good when I satisfy my needs. I’ll do whatever it takes to survive.
page-better-life-framework-level-2-descr: Life is about pleasing others (or the gods) so that they give us what we need.
page-better-life-framework-level-2-unloc: I can’t always survive on my own. I’ll seek the support of others to help meet my needs.
page-better-life-framework-level-3-descr: Life is about getting what I want by taking or creating advantages for myself.
page-better-life-framework-level-3-unloc: I feel good when I get what I want. I chase the next “win” so I can constantly feel good.
page-better-life-framework-level-4-descr: Life is about knowing what's right and what's wrong and making sure others do the right thing, too.
page-better-life-framework-level-4-unloc: I want to know that my life has meaning and that my actions are contributing to something greater than momentary wins.
page-better-life-framework-level-5-descr: Life is about knowing how to make good things happen, keeping the benefits, and always improving.
page-better-life-framework-level-5-unloc: I’m creating processes that ensures good things happen consistently for everyone and improve them as we go along.
page-better-life-framework-level-6-descr: Life is about being free to be whoever we are. If we stopped telling others what to do, we would have world peace.
page-better-life-framework-level-6-unloc: Systems don’t always work. It might be better if we stopped telling each other what to do and spent time to understand ourselves better instead.
page-better-life-framework-level-7-descr: Life is about drawing boundaries, saying no is for the best. Who I am and what I want changes often.
page-better-life-framework-level-7-unloc: Everyone should be free to be themselves, but we also need to protect ourselves. Saying no when it’s necessary is best for us and for society.
page-better-life-framework-level-8-descr: Life is an experiment. All we can do is the best that we know, so we should all know more.
page-better-life-framework-level-8-unloc: We may know what people want, but we can only guess why they want it until we ask more questions. All we can do is the best we know—so we should all know more.
page-better-life-framework-level-9-descr: Life is about learning where and how to shine the light. I am not the main character, I am just the spotlight. What is revealed is what I illuminate.
page-better-life-framework-level-9-unloc: Leveling up our perspectives is an ongoing process shaped by our experiences. We are all on our own journey, and all we can do is love everyone as they are.
page-better-life-framework-perspective-1: Unlocked from birth, we seek to satisfy our basic needs—like food, water, shelter, and sleep.
Since infancy, we recognize the presence of others and our dependence on them for satisfying our basic needs.
After our basic needs are consistently met, we identify other pursuits in life that can make us feel good—our wants, which we realize can differ from person to person.
As the positive feelings of satisfying our wants diminish over time, we crave a deeper sense of meaning and purpose that can give us a lasting feeling of happiness.
We question the reliability of relying on people and purpose to make decisions; instead, we seek measured, rational, and logical approaches to help everyone get what they want.
We recognize the limitations of our systems and identify the need for adaptability and personal judgment.
We understand what’s truly important to us and identify the boundaries necessary to safeguard our values.
With abundant time and psychological safety, we can be patient and intellectually curious with people who push our boundaries instead of simply reacting defensively.
As we observe the evolution of our perspectives and those of others, we come to appreciate that everyone sees the world in their own way and grows at their own pace.
page-better-life-framework-perspective-2: Our actions are driven by immediate physical sensations and needs. If our body needs it, we’ll take it or do it.
We notice that others have senses, desires, and feelings, and respond to what we see in others to get what we need.
No one is going to look out for our wants better than we can, so we have to make sure we get what we want.
We want to feel like we belong and are part of something much bigger than ourselves. We develop our beliefs and find like-minded people who share similar goals as us.
We want to control outcomes to make sure life gets better over time, and move on to solving bigger problems.
We become aware of our vast differences and strive to make everyone feel accommodated through rejection of structure.
We see how systems are related, interdependent, and where they are synergistic or clashing. We strive to create harmony among all systems.
We notice that the stories we tell ourselves shape the way we think and feel about the world. We want to learn more about the perspectives that cause others to think and feel differently than we do.
What is revealed is what we illuminate, and we are learning where and how to shine the light. We observe, understand, protect, honor, and love all forms of life and phenomena.
page-better-life-framework-perspective-3: Like hunger driving us to eat, our basic needs dictate our actions—pushing us to satisfy ourselves via the path of least resistance.
We understand reciprocal relationships and attempt to satisfy the needs of others (people, animals, nature, etc.) to ensure our needs are met.
We unlock our desires and focus on actions that feel rewarding. We involve others when they can help us get what we want.
In our search for meaning, we want to be sure that what we want and believe in is the right thing. So, we share passionately about our beliefs and defend them at all costs.
We create and use systems (workflows, processes, etc.)to optimize our lives and help people work together. Focus is on the scientific method and measurable outcomes.
We embrace freedom and individual expression, often rejecting strict conventional structures and traditions. We recognize that we barely even know ourselves, so how can we tell others what to do?

Everyone has values that are important to them, and these should be respected as long as they do not infringe on the values of others. By setting boundaries, we can maintain order and protect personal and collective well-being.
Some people in our lives won’t respect our boundaries. When we take the time to understand why, we can learn something new and in turn, help them feel heard and be more open to working it out.
With a deeper understanding of perspective thinking, we improve our awareness of the perspectives that drive us at any moment and recognize our power to shift our focus and change our perspective.
page-better-life-framework-perspective-4: Small survival bands (~100,000 years ago). We were transient and disorganized, driven only by instinct and focused on survival and immediate needs.
Small to medium settlements (~50,000 years ago). We were bound by rituals and belief in magic, with our social groups led by shamans or elders.
Exploitative empires ruled by force (~10,000 years ago). It was hierarchical, with power concentrated at the top.
Nation-states, religious orders (~5,000 years ago). Structured governance emerged, with roles and rules that provided a sense of purpose and order.
Capitalist democracies and market-driven meritocracies (beginning ~1600s). Individual success, progress, and market forces drove societal changes.
Social democracies (beginning ~1800s). Our focus was on inclusion and collaboration—valuing human rights and well-being of all.
Interconnected social web (~mid-1900s). Global issues were addressed by embracing our diversity while imposing the necessary restrictions.

Collective individualism (~late 1900s). We were deeply aware of our interconnectedness and act with the well-being of the world in mind. We accepted our experiences as part of a larger, unified whole.
Not formed yet. It will be a society built on empathy and unconditional love, where we understand and accept each other as we are.
